name: Acute Pharyngitis

likely: Group A Streptococcus (Streptococcus pyogenes) — when Centor score is high
possible: Fusobacterium necrophorum (consider in older adolescents/young adults with severe symptoms)
pathogens.why: Most pharyngitis is viral. Group A Streptococcus becomes a relevant consideration only with sufficient Centor criteria, and testing (rapid antigen detection or culture) should confirm before treating to avoid unnecessary antibiotic exposure.

investigations.test: Rapid antigen detection test (RADT) or throat culture
investigations.why: Confirms or excludes Group A Streptococcus before committing to antibiotics, directly preventing unnecessary use in viral pharyngitis.

references: IDSA Group A Streptococcal Pharyngitis Guidelines
reasonSource: e=>{const i=e._centor||0;return i>=3?`Centor score of ${i}/4 (fever, tonsillar exudate, tender cervical lymphadenopathy, absence of cough) raises probability of Group A Streptococcal pharyngitis. Throat swab/rapid antigen testing is recommended to confirm before committing to antibiotics, per stewardship principles — empiric treatment without testing is discouraged outside high Centor scores with epidemiologic risk.`:`Centor score of ${i}/4 is low, favoring a viral etiology. Antibiotics are not indicated at this time; testing (rapid strep/throat culture) should guide therapy if clinical suspicion for Group A Streptococcus persists.`}
